references.note: Shipped siblings in row order: orc-berserker, orc-elite-fighter, orc-master-wyrmic, fiery-orc-wyrmic, icy-orc-wyrmic, orc-high-pyromancer, orc-high-cryomancer, golbug, massok. Structural boss distinction, not colour-only; do not copy their anatomy.

prompt_fields.subject: A GREEN ORC BATTLEMASTER with bare green tusked head, small iron brow helmet with three short attached spikes, immense muscular broad shoulders and exposed green forearms. Spiked BLACK IRON ARMOUR: broad blackened plate segments with worn broad bright ash-silver upper faces, dense short steel spikes on shoulders, blocky ribbed chest plates, heavy square knee guards and a short segmented armoured skirt. ONE massive notched HEAVY BLADE held LOW HORIZONTALLY in both hands, across the body. Low wide planted squat stance; compact triangular silhouette from two broad spiked shoulders down to small waist, huge angular weapon bar in front. Native green skin is prominent on head and both arms; preserve blackened armour material using thin dark seams and broad pale rubbed steel planes for readability. This is not an obese belly like KraTor, no shield/upright sword like Ukruk, no wings/scale/polearm like Gorbat, no paired hammers like golbug, no horned skull/cleaver like massok. Broad shoulder-spike comb and horizontal notched blade distinct at 48px. Solid opaque material, no translucent areas.
prompt_fields.contrast: Boss identity through the specified body proportions, structural anatomy, equipment and pose; never just recolour the shipped siblings. No faction rings, health, shield, rank marks, selection, text or numbers.
prompt_fields.composition: One compact complete creature on a single circular tabletop disc, steep overhead three-quarter camera; visible clear neutral base ring on every side. Keep all anatomy and equipment well inside the inner four-fifths of disc radius. Base brightness must visually match reference neutral disc, with no illumination spill or ground effects. Disc plate discipline: measured results show generations of this style reference tend to render the disc DARKER than the reference, never lighter. So do not darken the disc at all: render the neutral disc -- including the whole outer-sixth ring band and the area under the creature -- at reference lightness, a hair lighter, never darker (the style reference's own brightness). No warm cast, glow, bounce-light, gradient or vignette anywhere on the disc. Do not darken the creature to compensate either. Add no warm cast, glow, bounce-light, gradient or vignette to the disc anywhere, including directly under or behind dark-bodied creatures. The ENTIRE creature, every limb, tail, wing, drip, staff and effect included, fits inside a circle of about three quarters of the disc radius around the disc centre, leaving a wide bare charcoal ring of base plate on every side, yet the creature is large and bold inside that circle. Draw the creature COMPACT and chunky: limbs, weapons, tools, cloth and effects are pulled in so the whole silhouette forms one rounded mass inside the inner three quarters of the disc; no tip, blade, hat brim, tentacle end, antenna or tail reaches the outer sixth ring band or crosses the disc rim. Value discipline (measured lesson from earlier tokens, including a rejected dark war dog and drem master): the creature's large masses are MID-LIGHT to LIGHT in value, clearly LIGHTER than the charcoal disc, with broad pale highlight planes on every upper-left surface and a thin bright LIGHT RIM along the outline, so the silhouette reads as a bright shape on the dark disc at very small size. Nothing near-black except tiny eye slits and thin seams; no large unlit black masses; blackened iron armour must have broad ash-silver lit surfaces. CALIBRATION FROM EARLIER TOKENS (first generations failed the disc-geometry and base-lightness gates because arms, weapons, tails and effects crossed the rim or the body shaded the plate): draw the whole creature clearly SMALLER than feels natural, everything inside a circle of about 0.55 of the disc radius, centred, with a wide bare ring of plate on every side; hold every weapon, limb, tail, wing and effect tight against the body; render the WHOLE disc, its outer ring band and the plate under and around the creature, at exactly the style reference lightness or a hair lighter, evenly all round, with no cast shadow, contact shadow or darkening beside the creature. DARK-SUBJECT DISCIPLINE (the native art of this creature is almost black; earlier near-black tokens were rejected at 48px): render it in MID-LIGHT slate and ash values, never black, at least as light as the copper-grey bevel of the disc and clearly lighter than the charcoal plate, with a thin bright pale RIM LIGHT along the whole upper-left outline and bright accent patches (named in the brief) so that the silhouette reads as a light shape on the dark disc at 48 pixels.
prompt_fields.palette: Green orc skin with light olive highlights; blackened iron armour with large worn silver lit planes and short ivory-steel spikes, black only in thin seams. Unchanged neutral charcoal/copper-grey disc, no lighting spill. Body mean luminance must meet the unchanged 65 floor.
